title: Exceptions in async methods (faulted tasks vs async void)
hook: A throw after await does not unwind the original caller's stack the way a synchronous method does. It faults the Task. async void has no Task, so the exception has nowhere safe to go.

blocks.text: When an async Task method throws, the exception is stored on the returned Task — not propagated synchronously to the caller. The first await of that Task rethrows the original exception (not wrapped in AggregateException the way Task.Wait does). async void methods have no Task to observe, so exceptions are posted to the SynchronizationContext or thread pool and can crash the process. OperationCanceledException is a separate type from business failures — catch it separately during shutdown.

entries.plainDefinition: A Task whose operation threw an exception. The exception is stored until someone awaits or inspects .Exception.
An async method returning void. Exceptions cannot be caught by the caller. Only acceptable for UI event handlers.
entries.example: private async void OnClick(object s, EventArgs e) { ... }

entries.plainDefinition: Thrown when a CancellationToken is signaled. Treat as cooperative shutdown, not a business failure.
Wraps multiple exceptions. Task.Wait and Task.Result throw this; await does not.
entries.example: task.Wait(); // throws AggregateException, not the inner exception

blocks.text: In a message consumer, an unobserved exception means a lost ack and silent data loss. Returning Task from handlers lets the host await, log, and nack the message. async void on a RabbitMQ Received event handler is how processes die on a JSON parse error the host never saw. Distinguishing cancellation from business failures prevents treating a graceful shutdown as a poison message.

blocks.title: Observation rule
blocks.body: Every async Task must be awaited or have a continuation that logs faults. Fire-and-forget without error handling is a production incident waiting to happen.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Throw inside async Task method
items.body: The exception is captured and stored on the returned Task. The caller's synchronous code continues.

items.title: Caller awaits the Task
items.body: await rethrows the original exception with its stack trace preserved.

items.title: Caller uses .Wait() or .Result
items.body: The exception is wrapped in AggregateException — a different catch path.

items.title: async void throws
items.body: No Task exists. Exception is posted to SynchronizationContext or thread pool — often unobserved.

diagram.title: Exception observation paths
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  T[Exception in async method] --> R{Return type?}
  R -->|Task / Task T| F[Stored on Task]
  F --> A[await rethrows inner exception]
  F --> W[Wait Result wraps AggregateException]
  R -->|async void| V[Posted to context or pool]
  V --> U[Unobserved — may crash process]

snippet.label: Observe faults in a message consumer
snippet.explanation: The host can await HandleAsync and log. An async void Received handler would ack or nack after an exception the host never saw.

snippet.label: await vs Wait — different exception wrapping
snippet.explanation: This is why .Result and .Wait() are dangerous beyond blocking — they change the exception type you catch.

snippet.label: Task.WhenAll with multiple failures
snippet.explanation: await WhenAll throws the first exception. Inspecting individual tasks reveals all faults.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: async void on a message Received event, then wondering why the process dies on a JSON error. Catching Exception around an await that also swallows OperationCanceledException during shutdown. Assuming try/catch around Task.Run without await observes the inner exception. Using .Result instead of await and getting AggregateException instead of the real type.

interviewTakeaways: await rethrows the inner exception; Wait/Result wrap in AggregateException.
async void cannot be awaited or unit-tested as a Task and is banned outside events.
Cancellation is an exception type; treat it as shutdown, not as a poison message by default.
commonPitfalls: async void on a RabbitMQ Received event, then wondering why the process dies on a JSON error.
catch (Exception) around an await that also swallows OperationCanceledException during SIGTERM.
Assuming try/catch around Task.Run without await observes the inner exception.

jsTsCorrelations.note: An async JS function always returns a Promise, so a throw becomes a rejection you can await. async void is closer to an unhandled rejection with no Promise handle — worse than JS because the caller cannot attach .catch.
